config.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow

intro.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple login form that authenticates a user using a cookie-based authentication flow. You will learn how to send user credentials to a mock server and handle the secure cookie it returns. The core programming concept involves managing authentication state and making HTTP requests. You will use Vue's reactive state, event handlers, and the Fetch API to implement this common web security pattern.
intro.usecase: Cookie-based authentication is the backbone of user sessions in countless web applications, from e-commerce sites like Amazon to social platforms like Facebook. As a developer, you'll implement this flow to manage secure login/logout in admin dashboards, customer portals, and SaaS products, where users expect to stay logged in across visits. This pattern handles sensitive operations—like updating profiles or accessing paid content—by automatically sending credentials with each request, ensuring a seamless and secure user experience without manual token management.

objectives: Implement a Vue component that renders a login form with email and password fields
Configure a Vue method to handle form submission and send authentication credentials to an API endpoint
Initialize reactive state to manage authentication status and user data in a Vue application
Construct HTTP request interceptors to automatically attach cookies to outgoing API calls
Apply conditional rendering to display different UI elements based on the user's authentication state
Integrate cookie-based authentication checks within Vue lifecycle hooks to protect routes
Manipulate browser cookies to store and retrieve authentication tokens after successful login

steps.title: Import Vue, ref, and reactive
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, and reactive from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and its reactivity helpers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue, ref, and reactive from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building the authentication flow.
successCriteria: Vue, ref, and reactive are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some items, but make sure to import Vue, ref, AND reactive from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue, ref, and reactive from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'AuthFlow' using the <script setup> syntax.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> block to define your component. This is where you'll write your component logic.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: a simple Vue component
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue, ref, and reactive from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Vue component structure with <script setup> and <template> sections.
successCriteria: The component is named 'AuthFlow' and uses <script setup> syntax with template section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the <script setup> syntax and have both script and template sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component named 'AuthFlow' using <script setup> syntax with both script and template blocks.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use ref to create a reactive state variable named isAuthenticated and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Remember to use the ref function imported from 'vue' to create reactive state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive state variable
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive isAuthenticated state variable is created with an initial value of false.
successCriteria: The isAuthenticated variable is declared using ref and initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref and initializing isAuthenticated to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a reactive state variable named isAuthenticated with an initial value of false using ref.

steps.title: Initialize user data state
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use the reactive function to create a user object with username and email properties. Initialize both properties with empty strings.
steps.hint: Call reactive with an object containing username and email keys, each set to an empty string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive user object is created with username and email properties, ready to store authentication data.
successCriteria: The user object is created using reactive() and contains username and email properties initialized as empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using reactive() to create an object with both username and email properties as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The user object wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use reactive() with an object containing username and email properties.

steps.title: Create login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, create a function named handleLogin that sets isAuthenticated to true and updates userData with a sample user object.
steps.hint: Define a function that modifies the reactive state variables you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogin function is defined that changes authentication state and populates user data.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function sets isAuthenticated to true and updates userData with at least name and email properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function sets isAuthenticated to true and updates userData with sample user information.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login handler isn't complete. Create a function named handleLogin that sets isAuthenticated to true and populates userData.

steps.title: Create logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the component, create a function named logout that sets isAuthenticated to false and clears userData by setting it to null.
steps.hint: Define a function that updates both reactive state variables to simulate logging out.
steps.expectedOutcome: A logout function is defined that resets authentication state and user data.
successCriteria: The logout function sets isAuthenticated to false and userData to null or an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a logout function, but it needs to set both isAuthenticated to false and clear userData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout function is missing or doesn't properly reset the authentication state and user data.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a main container div with class 'auth-container' and include an h1 heading with the text 'Cookie Authentication Demo'.
steps.hint: Add a div element with the class attribute and an h1 element inside it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: basic container with heading

My App
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a structured container with a descriptive heading.
successCriteria: A div with class 'auth-container' and an h1 with the text 'Cookie Authentication Demo' are present in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the div with class 'auth-container' and the h1 heading with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main container structure is missing or incorrect. Add a div with class 'auth-container' containing an h1 with 'Cookie Authentication Demo'.

steps.title: Display authentication status
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current authentication status. Use the isAuthenticated ref value to show either 'Logged in' or 'Logged out'.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or v-if/v-else to conditionally display text based on isAuthenticated.value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional text display in Vue

{{ isVisible ? 'Visible' : 'Hidden' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph that dynamically displays 'Logged in' or 'Logged out' based on the current authentication state.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that conditionally displays authentication status text using isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it doesn't yet conditionally display based on isAuthenticated. Try using a ternary operator or v-if/v-else.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element with conditional authentication status display is missing. Add a

tag that shows 'Logged in' or 'Logged out' based on isAuthenticated.

steps.title: Display user information when authenticated
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering inside the auth-container div to display user information only when isAuthenticated is true. Use a v-if directive to show a div containing the user's username and email.
steps.hint: Use v-if="isAuthenticated" on a div element to conditionally render content. Inside that div, display userData.username and userData.email.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a v-if directive that conditionally renders user information when the user is authenticated.
successCriteria: A div with v-if="isAuthenticated" is added inside the auth-container, displaying userData.username and userData.email.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some conditional rendering, but make sure you're using v-if="isAuthenticated" and displaying both username and email from userData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering for user information isn't quite right. Remember to use v-if with isAuthenticated and display userData properties.

steps.title: Add login button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Login' inside the main container, and wire its click event to call the login function.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call the login function when the button is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Login' button appears in the UI that, when clicked, triggers the login function to update authentication state.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Login' is present in the template, and its @click event is wired to the login function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it calls the login function when clicked using @click.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly wired to the login function. Check the template structure and event binding.

steps.title: Add logout button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a logout button inside the template that calls the logout function when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with the text 'Logout' and use @click to bind it to the logout function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="logout">Logout</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a logout button that triggers the logout function when clicked.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Logout' is added to the template and its click event is wired to the logout function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and click handler. Check that it uses @click="logout".
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout button is missing or not properly wired. Add a button element with @click="logout" and text 'Logout'.

steps.title: Style the authentication interface
steps.instruction: Add a <style> section at the end of your Vue component to style the authentication interface with CSS rules for the container, buttons, and user info display.
steps.hint: You can add a <style> tag after the closing </template> tag. Write CSS rules for .auth-container, h1, .user-info, .auth-button, and .logout-button classes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A <style> section is added with CSS rules that style the authentication interface elements.
successCriteria: The component includes a <style> section with CSS rules for .auth-container, h1, .user-info, .auth-button, and .logout-button classes (or similar selectors).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a <style> section, but some CSS rules might be missing or incomplete. Make sure to style the container, heading, user info, and buttons.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling section is missing or doesn't contain the expected CSS rules. Please add a <style> section with CSS rules for the authentication interface elements.
